I've saved the Q3 answers to `answer.json`. They haven't been checked against your Q2 reference values, because the project's CLAUDE.md says not to run checks or compare against example values.

| Item | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest net sales | `consumer`, 371,022,493 won |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 292 |
| c. Category with highest net sales | `svc`, 297,163,608 won |
| d. Month with highest net sales | `2025-09` |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | `u4@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 272 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 704,391 won |
| h. September vs. August growth | 36.9% (249,662,364 → 341,846,175 won) |

**How I handled the data:**
- **Segment names:** the same segment appears with different capitals and stray spaces (e.g. `" consumer"`, `"Enterprise "`). I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Order dates:** dates are stored in UTC, so I used UTC to decide which orders fall from July 1 to September 30.
- **Refunds:** the database has none for items that don't exist, and no refunded quantity is larger than the quantity ordered.
- **Duplicate emails:** 47 emails are shared by 2–3 customer records, often with different segments. I counted each customer ID as a separate customer for b, e and f. If a customer should mean one email instead, b, e and f could change.

The quickest way to settle the duplicate-email question is to run the same queries on Q2 and see whether they give your reference values (236 customers, `u43@ex.com`, 199 repeat customers). I left that out because of the CLAUDE.md rule.
